results.claim: Redbelly is a layer 1 blockchain built for real world asset tokenisation.
results.quote: The Redbelly Network is a layer 1 blockchain, built and optimised for real world asset tokenisation.

results.claim: Redbelly is a public network.
results.quote: No. Redbelly is a public network

results.claim: Asset types include bonds, (private) credit and real estate.
results.quote: TREASURIES & BONDS PRIVATE CREDIT CARBON CREDITS DERIVATIVES & COMMODITIES INSURANCE REAL ESTATE

results.claim: Assets are issued and traded as tokens.
results.quote: Enabling asset issuers to tokenise and trade compliant onchain structured products

results.claim: Every participant on the network is identity verified.
results.quote: all network participants are known. We enforce mandatory identity verification for all network participants

results.claim: Final in seconds: DBFT consensus makes transactions final within seconds.
results.quote: transactions are confirmed as irreversible within seconds

results.claim: No forks: the chain cannot fork.
results.quote: It cannot fork

results.claim: Ethereum compatible: runs Solidity smart contracts and Ethereum tools.
results.quote: allows Redbelly Network to support a diverse ecosystem of smart contracts, dApps, tools, and service providers

results.claim: Solidity developers can build on it.
results.quote: the largest pool of developers already proficient in the Solidity programming language

results.claim: Born at the University of Sydney, developed with CSIRO.
results.quote: Redbelly was born at the University of Sydney

results.claim: Developed in partnership with CSIRO (and its Data61).
results.quote: developed with The University of Sydney and CSIRO’s Data61

results.claim: Tokenisation records ownership as digital tokens and lets the asset's rules be programmed.
results.quote: Tokenisation records ownership of financial products and services as digital tokens, and lets you program the rules of the asset.

results.claim: Today: separate systems to reconcile; a (corporate) bond trade can take 2 to 4 business days to settle.
results.quote: take two to four business days to settle, because the asset record, the payment instruction, and the legal documentation typically live on different systems operated by different institutions

results.claim: Tokenised: one shared record.
results.quote: Establish digital registries as a shared source of truth across issuers, managers, and investors.

results.claim: Tokenised: one record shared by every party in the value chain.
results.quote: using a verifiable, single source of truth across the entirety of the value chain

results.claim: Tokenised: asset and payment swap in one step.
results.quote: a single atomic transaction can exchange both simultaneously

results.claim: Today: manual checks, breaches often found late (after the trade).
results.quote: Investor eligibility, holder limits and transfer restrictions are typically managed through spreadsheets, emails and manual sign-offs. Breaches are often identified after the trade

results.claim: Tokenised: checked before every trade.
results.quote: each trade is checked against your fund's rules before execution

results.claim: Tokenised: lower investment thresholds.
results.quote: lowering investment thresholds

results.claim: Tokenised: fractions (fractional ownership), traded 24/7.
results.quote: Holders gain fractional ownership, direct custody, atomic settlement, and 24/7 secondary trading through protocol finance.

results.claim: DBFT stands for Democratic Byzantine Fault Tolerant consensus.
results.quote: Democratic Byzantine Fault Tolerant (DBFT) consensus

results.claim: DBFT is leaderless.
results.quote: As a leaderless consensus algorithm, it eliminates single points of failure

results.claim: Classical blockchains: nodes compete, one block wins, the rest is wasted.
results.quote: This is a waste of resources as only one participant succeeds and the rest fail.

results.claim: DBFT: nodes cooperate and combine transactions into a superblock.
results.quote: combining distinct sets of transactions into a ‘superblock’ in a leaderless manner

results.claim: Redbelly consensus is collaborative instead of competitive.
results.quote: Redbelly consensus is collaborative instead of competitive

results.claim: No leader: every node plays a similar role.
results.quote: each node plays a similar role in the execution of the consensus

results.claim: No forks: once decided, a block is final.
results.quote: It cannot fork and has been mathematically proven to be correct through a process of formal verification through parameterised model checking

results.claim: Fault tolerant: proven (by model checking) safe while fewer than 1 in 3 nodes are faulty.
results.quote: for any number n of processes and any number f < n/3 of Byzantine processes

results.claim: Proven: the verification covers safety (and liveness) for any parameter.
results.quote: we formally verify, for any parameter, not only the safety properties of the Redbelly Blockchain consensus but also its liveness

results.claim: Receptor is Redbelly's native identity and verifiable credential protocol.
results.quote: Receptor is Redbelly's native digital identity and verifiable credential protocol.

results.claim: It makes sure everyone on the network is who they say they are.
results.quote: ensuring that all network participants are who they say they are

results.claim: Network access needs a credential from an accredited issuer.
results.quote: Only accredited issuers can issue credentials that give users network access.

results.claim: Apps state who qualifies.
results.quote: helps use case developers to surface the eligibility criteria for their real world asset tokenisation use case

results.claim: Example criterion: accredited investor status.
results.quote: proving their age, address, or accredited investor status

results.claim: Users prove they qualify without uploading documents.
results.quote: Users can prove their eligibility without having to upload documents or share sensitive personal information with your platform.

results.claim: Built on the W3C verifiable credential data model.
results.quote: Receptor is built on the W3C verifiable credential data model

results.claim: Three roles: Issuer, Holder, Verifier.
results.quote: The framework is composed of three essential modules; the Issuer, the Holder, and the Verifier.

results.claim: The issuer issues the credential.
results.quote: Issuer: Use to define and issue verifiable credentials to users.

results.claim: The holder keeps it in a wallet.
results.quote: acquire and store verifiable credentials

results.claim: The verifier checks the proof and the issuer's signature.
results.quote: checks its mathematical validity against the trusted issuer's public key

results.claim: A cryptographic signature confirms authenticity.
results.quote: along with a cryptographic signature, allowing them to confirm its authenticity

results.claim: Credentials are reusable.
results.quote: Reusable client identity and KYC credentials streamline onboarding and reduce duplication

results.claim: Your data is not copied to every app (no duplicate stores of it).
results.quote: user data is kept at the edge and is not duplicated across each service provider which would create many honeypots of sensitive data

results.claim: A ZK proof shows something is true without revealing the data behind it.
results.quote: uses zero-knowledge proofs, allow users to prove a statement is true without revealing any of the underlying data that makes it true

results.claim: Ask: an app asks one yes or no question (example on the artwork: over 18?).
results.quote: The verifier asks a yes/no question using a query, like “Is the user over 18?”

results.claim: Prove: your wallet proves it (generates the proof); nothing is revealed.
results.quote: The user's wallet generates a cryptographic proof that they satisfy the query, without revealing their address or any other personal information.

results.claim: Artwork: the passport credential's fields stay hidden; the birth date is queried, not revealed.
results.quote: can be queried against a relative date, rather than being revealed

results.claim: Check: a smart contract on Redbelly verifies it.
results.quote: where a smart contract verifies its validity

results.claim: Artwork: the result is true or false, with no personal data on chain.
results.quote: with no personal data ever being exposed on-chain

results.claim: Selective disclosure reveals only the fields asked for.
results.quote: Selective Disclosure (SD) is a method where a user reveal only specific fields from their credential to a verifier.

results.claim: Zero knowledge reveals no data, only the proof.
results.quote: In SD, data is revealed. In PBQ, only the proof is shared

results.claim: Tokeniser is a Redbelly Network project.
results.quote: Tokeniser is a Redbelly Network project

results.claim: It runs on Redbelly Network.
results.quote: Tokeniser operates on Redbelly Network

results.claim: Registry, investor portal and API.
results.quote: Program the rules of your asset, with admin tools, an investor portal, and an API for automations and build-your-own portals.

results.claim: For funds, shares (equities), loans and notes.
results.quote: End-to-end management of funds, equities, loans and notes.

results.claim: Stack: Tokeniser issues, Averer reaches, Redbelly Network settles.
results.quote: Compliant issuance and lifecycle of tokenised assets.

results.claim: Averer: identity and wallet; credentials gate every holder.
results.quote: Identity and the AI-native wallet. Verifiable credentials gate every holder

results.claim: Redbelly Network settles; final the moment it completes.
results.quote: final the moment it completes

results.claim: Every holder verified and every transfer checked, automatically.
results.quote: Every holder is verified and every transfer checked against the asset's rules, automatically.

results.claim: An asset can carry its own rules (compliance becomes a property of the asset).
results.quote: This transforms the complexity of compliance assurance into an inherent property of the assets themselves.

results.claim: Only eligible parties can hold the token.
results.quote: only parties that can prove their eligibility will be able to hold the token

results.claim: Checks: identity, eligibility and limits, before the trade. Failing trades do not proceed. Every check is logged.
results.quote: Before any trade proceeds, the investor's identity, eligibility (including wholesale or sophisticated status where required) and your limits are verified automatically. Trades that fail a check do not proceed, and every check is logged.

results.claim: Eligibility is enforced at the point of trade.
results.quote: defined investor eligibility, enforced at the point of trade

results.claim: Set by the issuer in line with its licence and mandate.
results.quote: embed turnkey jurisdictional compliance, according to their license and mandate, into their tokenised assets directly

results.claim: Rules carry over when assets meet other apps on the network.
results.quote: when different tokenised assets and protocols interact on our network, they automatically inherit the compliance properties of the underlying assets

results.claim: Every participant is known.
results.quote: an innovative identity layer that ensures all network participants are known

results.claim: A node that cheats leaves proof it cannot deny.
results.quote: Think of these as digital fingerprints that cannot be denied.

results.claim: Participants are verified by accredited credential issuers.
results.quote: We enforce mandatory identity verification for all network participants through our marketplace of accredited verifiable credential issuers.

results.claim: Each transaction ties back to a responsible party.
results.quote: all transactions can be tied back to a responsible entity

results.claim: Accountability at protocol level through proofs of fraud (Polygraph) and an identity layer.
results.quote: Accountability is enforced at a protocol level through a novel mechanism that constructs undeniable proofs of fraud

results.claim: A cheating node leaves signed traces that become proof of fraud.
results.quote: they leave cryptographically signed traces that honest nodes can combine to build undeniable proofs of fraud

results.claim: Faulty nodes are removed from consensus.
results.quote: an exclusion protocol to remove the identified faulty nodes from the consensus committee

results.claim: Polygraph is the first accountable Byzantine consensus algorithm.
results.quote: Polygraph, the first accountable Byzantine consensus algorithm

results.claim: Identities are verified while ZK proofs keep personal data private.
results.quote: Participants verify their identities, but their privacy remains protected through zero-knowledge proofs.

results.claim: The DAO decides by vote on its own platform.
results.quote: Signature voting on Redbelly. No gas, no subscription.

results.claim: Only identity verified wallets can vote.
results.quote: Every address here clears Redbelly’s passport-backed identity check.

results.claim: Verified wallets hold a Receptor credential.
results.quote: Only wallets holding a Receptor credential can vote, as Redbelly requires one for network access.

results.claim: Propose: posted on the platform, locked (cannot be edited) once open.
results.quote: a proposal cannot be edited once it is open

results.claim: Voting is signing a message: no transaction, no gas.
results.quote: you sign a message, you never send a transaction

results.claim: Voting costs no gas.
results.quote: Voting here costs no gas because nothing is ever sent to the chain.

results.claim: Voting power can be RBNT held.
results.quote: Voting power equals the native RBNT held at the snapshot block.

results.claim: Or one vote per verified address.
results.quote: One verified address, one vote

results.claim: Check: signed ballots anyone can re-check.
results.quote: Your signature is stored with your ballot, so anyone can re-verify that your vote was really yours without trusting this server.

results.claim: High Council: 3 seats elected July 2026.
results.quote: The High Council seats elected in July 2026

results.claim: Five pods (working groups).
results.quote: Five pods: Marketing, Builder/Develop, Researcher, Community and Partnerships.

results.claim: Treasury: new funding (new treasury-funded initiatives) paused until a future vote resumes it.
results.quote: New treasury-funded initiatives are suspended until a future governance vote resumes them. Existing approved obligations continue.

results.claim: Past Snapshot votes are imported on the platform.
results.quote: IMPORTED FROM SNAPSHOT
